propositions: The gate matches field names globally as bare attribute names, causing any field whose name is read on ANY unrelated config to pass the gate regardless of whether that field itself is ever read
A field with a commonly reused name (e.g. 'enabled', 'path', 'timeout') is at high risk of false-negative because the same name on an unrelated config can satisfy the gate
The fix must resolve reads to their OWNING dataclass rather than match bare attribute names, so a field is satisfied only by a read of an instance of its declaring class
After fixing the gate and running it across the whole schema, newly-flagged fields must be reported with accurate `# read-via:` markers naming real consumers, not silently exempted

Required negative fixtures (string-keyed reads like `ReconcilerConfig.lock_lease_secs` via getattr and `VerifyConfig` fields via gate_enabled string keys) must continue to pass with their existing markers
